:::{#def-model-kl-divergence}
#### Kullback--Leibler divergence between two parameter values

Let $\vX$ be a continuous random vector with density $\p(\vx \mid \param)$
for a scalar parameter $\param$,
and let $\param_0$ be the true parameter value.
The
[Kullback--Leibler divergence](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#def-kl-divergence)
of the model with parameter $\param$ from the model with parameter $\param_0$
is the expectation, under $\param_0$, of the log ratio of the two densities.
As a function of $\param$, it is written

$$
\kldivf{\param_0}{\param}
\eqdef \Expp_{\param_0}\sb{\log \frac{\p(\vX \mid \param_0)}{\p(\vX \mid \param)}}.
$$

:::
